OP-SWC-002.text: The phase offset inside the 10 ms control cycle at which the flow check and the watchdog cycle service run, and the numeric priority scheme, are not given by the inputs. The architecture fixes only that the refresh instants are one control period apart and after the flow check; the value is a design parameter.

OP-SWC-003.text: The inputs name no storage that survives software and watchdog resets but is cleared at a power-on reset (CON-SUP-003 lists none); follows OP-SYE-001. The architecture states the retained fault state SWC-SUP-054 and its driver interface SWC-SUP-026 independent of the medium.

OP-SWC-004.text: The CRC throughput at the configured core clock is not stated, so the chunk size that keeps each independent watchdog service interval well below 100 ms (DEC-SWC-004) cannot be fixed here; the margin and chunk size are design values.

OP-SWC-005.text: Handling of a non-integral period is closed at architecture level by DEC-SWC-015 (rejected as configuration fault 9 at start-up). What remains is only the numeric upper bound of a period, which is the width of the scheduler's per-entry tick counter and the period encoding of the configuration format; whatever width the design picks, validation uses it, so no accepted value is mistimed.

OP-SWC-006.text: CON-SUP-002 names RM0486 without a section or page, so no controlled hardware reference supports the GPIO access and reset properties (whether a single pin write is atomic, and the pin state from reset until configuration). OP-SWC-007.text: The number of characters the USART driver interface SWC-SUP-024 accepts per transmit call (its buffer depth) is not given. The deadline analysis of SWC-SUP-039 assumes a full report line of at most 40 characters is accepted per call or drained without waiting; the depth is a driver design value that must meet this.

OP-SWC-008.text: The maximum length of a task name used as entity in a fault report is not given. The 40 character report line limit of SWC-SUP-039 requires the configuration to limit the name length; the limit is a configuration design value.

OP-SWC-010.text: The inputs give no RAM, flash or stack limit (CON-SUP-004 only forbids dynamic allocation and recursion) and no device memory size, so no numeric stack or other memory budget can be allocated to the start-up task SWC-SUP-060 or to the other tasks. OP-SWC-013.text: SWR-DIA-001 requires every fault report within 10 ms of detection, and a line already started is completed first. If four reports are detected at one instant while an answer line is in progress, the fourth cannot complete within 10 ms (up to 12.9 ms, DEC-SWC-014). OP-SWC-014.text: The timer clock and prescaler are not given, so it is not established that the time base can run at the 10 us unit DEC-SWC-012 needs for the 100 us detection bound; the design confirms the unit at the configured clock or a finer unit is used.
